cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: The Approved Explanation
cards.instruction: Protect someone or the group by maintaining a simplified account that everyone can safely repeat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Grandad's embarrassed about the gazebo. We'll use one account for his birthday guests: the garden's unavailable, so we're celebrating indoors.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's told Aunt Jean he set it on fire. Do I contradict him?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. Everyone says, 'Everyone's fine; we're celebrating indoors.' I'll give him the same wording.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Jean wants the fire story in his speech. She's brought her trifle and expects a thank-you too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then he opens with our sentence and thanks her for the trifle. I'll introduce him that way. You ask Jean about her recipe while he starts serving; he doesn't owe the room another account.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 refuses B2 contradiction and dictates safe wording; A5 controls speech introduction and assigns B a diversion so Grandad repeats the same protective account rather than the fire story.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 existing fire disclosure causes A3 truthful current-state sentence; B4 speech and trifle thanks causes A5 same opening then food acknowledgment and recipe diversion.

relationship.evidence: B2 checks whether to contradict known facts; B4 reports two demands from Jean, supplying an actual alternative topic.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 thanks expectation to protect Grandad during the demanded speech, extending the shared account into a live social moment.

specificity.evidence: A1 birthday moved indoors after gazebo trouble; B2 fire known; B4 dessert and speech establish concrete family action.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 recipe diversion follows B4 trifle and avoids the first version forced gazebo-dessert joke.
